transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Triton CTO), Maya Lopez (ML Engineer), Olivia Chen (Product), Samir Rao (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Triton Dynamics' model selection constraints - context length, multilingual needs, tool-calling, and deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer is evaluating open models and wants a POC to validate latency/cost and security controls.

Topics: model families (Llama3, Mistral, Falcon), context length requirements (8k, 32k, 64k), multilingual support (Spanish, German, Japanese), tool-calling and function calling, deployment modes (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), security (SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS, VPC), benchmarking plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - Ethan from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:06] Daniel: Hi, Daniel Park, CTO at Triton Dynamics, we build nav systems for maritime - ML heavy.
[00:10] Maya: Maya, ML engineer, I'll be running the experiments.
[00:13] Olivia: Olivia, product lead, mostly here for timeline and success criteria.
[00:17] Samir: Samir, security - I'll focus on compliance and KMS/HSM questions.
[00:21] Priya: Priya Nair, solutions engineer at Redwood, I run the deep dives and benchmarks.
[00:26] Ethan: Great, main goal today is to figure out which model family and deployment mode fits your constraints. We know you mentioned context length for long maritime logs and some multilingual support - can you elaborate?
[00:38] Daniel: Yeah, so two main flows: first is near-real-time command summarization from sensor logs that are usually around 5-8k tokens but sometimes spike to 20-30k when we include long telemetry dumps. Second, offline analytics that can be 50-60k tokens. We also need Spanish and Japanese outputs for certain regions.
[00:55] Maya: For the real-time path, latency is important - sub 400ms token latency ideally, and cost needs to be predictable. Offline jobs can tolerate higher latency.
[01:04] Priya: Got it. For context length, there are trade-offs: models like Llama 3 variants and Mistral have strong instruction following and can be run at 32k contexts with certain kernels, Falcon has good throughput on some GPUs, and there are new 64k-capable variants but they're heavier. Have you benchmarked any of these?
[01:22] Daniel: We ran small tests with OpenAI as a baseline but want to move to open models for cost and control. We tried a Mistral-7B local but couldn't get stable 32k runs - memory spikes.
[01:33] Ethan: That's a common pattern. Redwood can help there - our runtime selects kernels and quantization profiles and we do automatic KV cache management to handle long contexts efficiently. For spikes we usually recommend a dedicated pool or private deployment for the longer offline jobs.
[01:46] Olivia: What's the difference in cost between hosted and dedicated for us? If we commit to reserved capacity, does that buy better latency?
[01:54] Ethan: Yes, dedicated capacity gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale; hosted is pay-as-you-go and simpler to start with. We'll send the pricing sheet, but ballpark: hosted for intermittent traffic, dedicated for steady high-throughput.
[02:06] Maya: On model selection, we need tool-calling - e.g., model must support function/tool calls for a retrieval pipeline and structured outputs. Do the open models support that?
[02:15] Priya: Most instruction-tuned open models support structured outputs, but tool/function calling is at the SDK/routing layer typically. Redwood supports function/tool calling on top of models - we have a shim that maps function calls to model structured outputs and does verification. Some models are better at reliably emitting JSON; we test that in the benchmark harness.
[02:33] Samir: Security - we are regulated, so SOC2, audit logs, SAML SSO, and KMS integration are required. For certain regions we may need VPC or on-prem. How does Redwood handle keys and logs?
[02:43] Ethan: Redwood Private offers customer-managed control plane with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs retention; Dedicated includes options for VPC peering and network isolation. For Hosted we support SSO/SAML and encrypted-at-rest with Redwood-managed KMS, but for HSM you'd want Private.
[02:58] Samir: And data residency? We have EU and APAC customers - can we pin region?
[03:03] Priya: Yes, with Dedicated and Private you can pin region; Hosted has regional endpoints for major clouds but less control. We'll map that in the POC.
[03:12] Maya: About model performance - we need both multilingual accuracy and long-context quality. Which models in your catalog do best?
[03:19] Priya: From our catalog: Llama 3 variants (instruction-tuned) are strong on instruction and multilingual with 32k options; Mistral 7B/ Mixtral family is cost-effective and good generalization; Falcon is throughput friendly; there are also emerging models like Gemma variants and MPT for some tasks. For 64k contexts, the model pool is smaller - often custom extended-position models or patched attention kernels plus KV caching. We can run the offline 64k jobs on Dedicated/Private with custom kernel selection.
[03:45] Daniel: We have a hard limit on cost per 1M tokens - do you have examples of per-token cost across models?
[03:50] Ethan: We'll share per-token estimates from our Optimize tool - it factors in batching, quantization, and hosting. That'll be in the pricing + benchmark pack.
[03:58] Olivia: Timeline - we want a short POC in two weeks to validate latency and output quality. Is that feasible?
[04:03] Priya: Yes, we typically do a 2-4 week POC. Week 1: baseline runs on hosted/dedicated (8k and 32k); Week 2: tool-calling and multilingual tests; if you want 64k offline runs that's part of week 3 depending on infra.
[04:18] Maya: For the POC, what do we need to provide?
[04:20] Ethan: Samples of your prompts and representative logs, success criteria (e.g., exactness of summaries, latency SLO), and security constraints. We'll provision a sandbox project and share credentials.
[04:30] Samir: For security docs, do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation plus an architecture diagram?
[04:34] Ethan: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 reports, our Security whitepaper, and the network diagrams for Dedicated/Private. Priya will attach a checklist of what we need for compliance review.
[04:44] Daniel: On fallback policies - if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can requests route to hosted or a smaller model?
[04:49] Priya: Absolutely - smart routing allows policies to failover to compatible variants or hosted endpoints. You can set cost vs latency tiers. For mission-critical paths we recommend canary and fallback policies to keep systems online.
[04:59] Maya: A couple of nitty-gritty items: quantized model fidelity - how consistent are outputs when moving from fp16 to 4-bit/8-bit quantization?
[05:07] Priya: We run model-specific regression tests in our Optimize pipeline. Some models degrade more than others; we report BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity against your test prompts. We'll include regression thresholds in the POC.
[05:17] Olivia: Stakeholders - who's the right person on Redwood to coordinate?
[05:20] Ethan: I'll be your AE and primary contact. Priya will run the technical POC. For security questions Samir can email our security team.
[05:27] Daniel: Great. One more - multilingual fine-tuning or instruction tuning? We may need to customize behavior for domain-specific marine terms.
[05:33] Priya: We support prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and light fine-tuning/adapter workflows depending on the deployment. For Hosted we often use RAG + prompt engineering; Dedicated/Private can support adapters and custom weights depending on license. We'll scope that in the POC.
[05:47] Ethan: Okay, quick recap of next steps - I'll send pricing and commitment options, Priya will share benchmark harness and run 8k/32k tests, and you'll share sample prompts and compliance needs.
[05:59] Daniel: Sounds good, thanks.
[06:01] Olivia: Thanks all.
[06:03] Ethan: We'll follow up with calendar invites for the POC kickoff.

End of transcript.

Notes/Artifacts Mentioned: pricing spreadsheet link (sent after call), benchmark harness doc (to be shared), sample prompts sheet (customer to provide), SOC2 and security docs link.
